title: Building Block Two: Creating the Framework for Cultural Change
coreMove: Redesign the consequences and conversations that teach people what the culture really values.
sourcePressure: Second building block: culture changes through operational consequences, rewards tied to performance, social software, robust dialogue, and the behavior leaders exhibit or tolerate. No chapter-specific company case is frozen.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treat culture as slogans, values statements, or morale work.

hook: the building block two: creating the framework for cultural change that nobody sees until it is too late
a meeting room where every plan sounds good
a generic promise colliding with reality
counterintuition: Most leaders think X, but the opposite is true
The problem is not effort, it is discipline
Execution is not about working harder
tryThisNow: set a timer and write three priorities
audit one goal in your notebook
ask yourself what matters most today
examples: generic project kickoff with vague owners
student team with a deadline and no specificity
family calendar scene used as a management analogy

exampleSpecs.domain: a public radio newsroom changing what wins airtime after rushed corrections
exampleSpecs.audience: an editor who wants cultural change without slogans
exampleSpecs.stakes: listeners lose trust if speed keeps outranking accuracy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan changes the praise at the editorial meeting from fastest filed segment to cleanest corrected segment and the newsroom starts chasing a different standard
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Megan four corrections in one pledge week to see what the applause had been teaching.

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional ambulance service where crews avoid reporting equipment faults
exampleSpecs.stakes: unreported faults can strand a crew during a call
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ben turns robust dialogue from open talk into the one uncomfortable question about why the fault tags are missing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Why are there no fault tags on a truck everyone complains about?" Ben asks, and the room goes quiet.

exampleSpecs.domain: a university dining hall where lateness is tolerated for popular station leads
exampleSpecs.stakes: students wait while tolerated behavior rewrites the standard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Margaux decides whether to excuse the popular lead again or make the tolerated behavior visible as the real rule
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 10:51 a.m., Margaux sees the omelet station closed while the brunch line curls past the tray return.

exampleSpecs.domain: a software security review team where bonuses favor shipped features over closed vulnerabilities
exampleSpecs.stakes: the reward system teaches engineers to leave risk unresolved
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chris rewrites the bonus note so closed critical vulnerabilities count in the same sentence as shipped features
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are holding the bonus memo, and the vulnerability column is still treated like a footnote.

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional swim club where parents demand fairness but celebrate only medal counts
exampleSpecs.stakes: young swimmers learn that development talk is less real than podium status
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ingrid predicts which behavior the awards night will teach, then changes the ceremony so improvement and relay discipline carry status
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What does a nine-year-old learn when every speech says effort and every trophy says medals?

exampleSpecs.domain: a warehouse safety committee where near-miss forms are treated as blame documents
exampleSpecs.stakes: workers hide signals that could prevent the next injury
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Yusuf traces the hidden near miss to the consequence attached to the form and changes the social software around reporting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The bent pallet jack handle sits behind the loading door with no form attached.

skillTargets: identify the actual reward or tolerance shaping culture
distinguish open talk from robust dialogue
choose consequences that operationalize a desired behavior
analyze how leader behavior becomes social software

tryThisNowSpec: Find one behavior you tolerate or reward today and write the rule it is teaching, whether or not you intended it.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
